display_name: Interpretation Act (Canada), R.S.C., 1985, c. I-21: the whole Act in L4 (time, commencement, resolutions, repeal, rules of reading, powers, definitions and the Schedule)

l4_bin.note: check.sh was run with L4_TARGET=unstable; the comparison with a main build was not made, because the encoding uses REFUSE, #ASSERT REFUSED, @lang and YMD, which a main build rejects. Pass 1 used another build (dev, sha256 2d912dd2a61ba36b3fb8c1e02dcbd445ba1143c3b8ecb931462c01050cd607d7).

seat: none; the Guide asks for a seat layer for the individual and this row has none (NOTES.md, section Seat)
expected_red_note: ten deliberately failing expectations, each written from the text and each a different way a plausible but wrong reading would answer; they are counted by check.sh (expected_failed = 10) and are kept to show the tests can fail.

scope.encoded: Every unit of the text except the title block, the headings, the Schedule heading and the short title (s 1) (inert, reasons 1 and 2) and six entries shown repealed; the Related Provisions item (1998, c. 30, s. 10), which pass 2 had filed as inert, is encoded since pass 3. The last day of a period of N days, months or years after, from or before a day (ss 27, 28, 37(1)); clear days; the day a thing may be done when the last day is a holiday (s 26, holidays supplied by the caller); when an Act, a regulation, a proclamation or an appointment binds or takes effect (ss 5, 6, 7, 18, 23), the precondition of s 5(4), the permission of s 7 to exercise a power before commencement, and the proceedings the Related Provisions item takes up; expiry (s 6(1)); age (s 30); calendar, financial and Dominical years (s 37); the time to lay a regulation before Parliament, the body each of the four expressions of s 39(1) names, which resolutions they require and what an annulment needs (s 39(1)); repeal, replacement, annulment and demise of the Crown (ss 2(2), 39(2), 43, 44, 46); standard time, local time and the time of day (ss 35(1), 29); the rules of reading (ss 3, 4, 5(1), 8 to 16, 18 to 22, 25, 32 to 34, 36, 38, 40 to 42, 45); the powers words imply (ss 23(4), 24, 31, 34.1); every defined term of ss 2(1) and 35(1), as a table with a rule for each (the terms, the word the Act uses, what it names, includes or excludes, what it points at); the Commonwealth Schedule (51 rows, each tested). Where the text does not answer, the encoding returns a named refusal and the tests assert it. Borrowed terms (the Bank Act, Oceans Act, Criminal Code, Constitution Act 1982, Statutory Instruments Act, National Defence Act, Canada Evidence Act) are asked as facts.

method: A single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone, in three passes (pass 1 on 2026-10-21; pass 2, the completion pass to whole, and pass 3, the corrections after an independent test pass, both on 2026-10-29), without subagents and without reading any other encoding of interpretation law. Expected values were written from the text and are in NOTES.md section 4 and in the test files beside the assertions; none was changed to match the code's output, except the two pass-1 assertions of a refusal that pass 3 corrected and logged in NOTES.md (Changes to existing modules).
not_reviewed: No domain expert, lawyer or second encoder has read this against the statute. The French version has not been consulted. The text is an unofficial rendering that has not been checked against the official consolidation. The quotation of the text in comments rests on the ruling recorded in STUB-SOURCE-LICENSE.md (2026-10-25); no human has checked that the quotation here keeps the notice and attribution it asks for. The 32 class A forks in NOTES.md section 3 have not been ruled on.
